# Executive Summary & Methodological Framework

<div class="summary-box">
<h3 style="margin-top: 0; color: #1e40af;">Scope of the Evidence Synthesis Framework</h3>
This report presents a fully reproducible frequentist Network Meta-Analysis (NMA) integrating 12 sequential analytical modules and 14 high-resolution 300 DPI exhibits adhering to PRISMA-NMA reporting guidelines. The pipeline combines graph-theoretical Laplacian estimation via <code>netmeta</code>, global variance decomposition, local node-splitting (<code>netsplit</code>), leave-one-out cross-validation across 24 randomized controlled trials, component deconstruction (CNMA), 10,000 Monte Carlo ranking simulations, bivariate benefit-risk modeling, and transitivity assessments.
</div>

### Evidence Base & Study Design
- **Clinical Setting:** First-line systemic therapies evaluated in adult patients with advanced disease.
- **Primary Endpoint:** Overall Survival (OS), quantified as Hazard Ratios ($\text{HR}$) with $95\%$ Confidence Intervals.
- **Secondary Safety Endpoint:** Grade 3–5 Severe Adverse Events, quantified as Odds Ratios ($\text{OR}$) with $95\%$ Confidence Intervals.
- **Evidence Base:** 24 randomized controlled trials encompassing **15,753 patients** (20 two-arm trials, 4 three-arm trials) and 14,357 safety-evaluable patients across 32 study contrasts.
- **Competing Therapeutic Regimens:**
  1. `Drug A`: Standard comparator / reference backbone anchor.
  2. `Drug B`: Active monotherapy.
  3. `Drug C`: Combination regimen (backbone + active agent).
  4. `Drug D`: Dual-combination regimen.
  5. `Drug E`: Targeted monotherapy.
  6. `Drug F`: Targeted combination regimen.
- **Constituent Components (CNMA):**
  - `Component A`: Reference backbone anchor.
  - `Component B`, `Component C`, `Component D`: Individual active therapeutic agents.

---

## Core Methodological Engines Implemented

<div class="highlight-box">
<h3 style="margin-top: 0; color: #065f46;">Key Analytical Modules:</h3>
<ol style="margin-bottom: 0; padding-left: 20px; line-height: 1.7;">
  <li><strong>Contrast Scale Transformation:</strong> Exact conversion of reported Hazard Ratios and 95% CIs to symmetric Gaussian log-hazard contrasts ($\text{TE} = \ln(\text{HR})$) and standard errors ($\text{seTE}$).</li>
  <li><strong>Multi-Arm Covariance Adjustment:</strong> Preservation of linear contrast additivity ($\text{TE}_{BC} = \text{TE}_{AC} - \text{TE}_{AB}$) and positive-definite covariance structure via <code>netmeta::chkmultiarm()</code>.</li>
  <li><strong>Graph-Theoretical Inversion:</strong> Implementation of electrical network theory (Rücker, 2012) via the Laplacian pseudoinverse ($L^+$), guaranteeing exact analytical weighted least squares solutions.</li>
  <li><strong>Orthogonal Inconsistency Testing:</strong> Decomposition of global variance ($Q = Q_{\text{het}} + Q_{\text{inc}}$), local node-splitting analysis (<code>netsplit</code>), and Net Heat leverage evaluation.</li>
  <li><strong>Leave-One-Out (LOO) Sensitivity:</strong> Systematic jackknife cross-validation across all 24 trials auditing estimate stability.</li>
  <li><strong>Component Network Meta-Analysis (CNMA):</strong> Deconstructing multi-agent regimens into constituent components and testing for pharmacological synergy ($Q_{\text{diff}}$ test).</li>
  <li><strong>Probabilistic Hierarchy & SUCRA:</strong> 10,000 Monte Carlo draws from the multivariate normal covariance matrix yielding discrete rank distributions and cumulative rankograms.</li>
  <li><strong>Bivariate Benefit-Risk Trade-Off Matrix:</strong> Concurrent synthesis of survival efficacy against severe adverse events across four decision quadrants.</li>
  <li><strong>Network Meta-Regression:</strong> Evaluating potential effect modification across publication year, sample size, and geographic setting.</li>
  <li><strong>Subgroup Network Meta-Analysis:</strong> Assessing geographic transitivity across regional cohorts with between-subgroups heterogeneity testing ($Q_{\text{bws}}$).</li>
  <li><strong>Minimal Clinically Important Difference (MCID):</strong> Calculating the posterior probability of achieving $\ge 20\%$ mortality reduction ($\text{HR} \le 0.80$).</li>
</ol>
</div>

# Mathematical Foundations of Network Meta-Analysis

## Contrast Data Representation for Survival Outcomes
In time-to-event outcomes, clinical trials report Hazard Ratios ($\text{HR}$) and $95\%$ Confidence Intervals $[\text{lower}, \text{upper}]$. Statistical synthesis is conducted on the natural logarithmic scale:

$$\text{TE}_i = \ln(\text{HR}_i), \quad \text{seTE}_i = \frac{\ln(\text{upper}_i) - \ln(\text{lower}_i)}{2 \times 1.96}$$

## Multi-Arm Trial Adjustments
In multi-arm trials with a shared control arm $A$, the covariance between contrasts $AB$ and $AC$ equals the variance of the baseline arm:

$$\text{Cov}(\text{TE}_{AB}, \text{TE}_{AC}) = \text{Var}(\text{Arm}_A)$$

Adjustment via `netmeta` ensures correct effective sample size and prevents unit-of-analysis error.

# Treatment Ranking Hierarchy (P-Scores)

Frequentist P-scores (Rücker & Schwarzer, 2015) quantify the probability that an intervention is superior to competing treatments:

$$P\text{-score}_i = \frac{1}{m-1} \sum_{j \neq i} \Phi\left(\frac{\widehat{\theta}_j - \widehat{\theta}_i}{\sqrt{\text{Var}(\widehat{\theta}_i - \widehat{\theta}_j)}}\right)$$

```{r fig_ranking, echo=FALSE, out.width="90%"}
knitr::include_graphics("../outputs/figures/03_pscore_ranking.png")
```

# Dual-Model League Table: Direct vs Network Synthesis

The league table presents all pairwise head-to-head comparisons across the evidence network.

```{r fig_league_table, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%", fig.align='center'}
knitr::include_graphics("../outputs/figures/07_league_table_figure.png")
```

### Reading Guide
- **Diagonal (Navy Badges):** Regimens ordered hierarchically by P-score from Rank 1 (`Drug C`) to Rank 6 (`Drug A`).
- **Lower Triangle (Green & Slate Tiles):** Random-effects NMA estimates ($\text{Column} \text{ vs } \text{Row}$). Green highlighting indicates statistically significant superiority ($p < 0.05$).
- **Upper Triangle (Blue Tiles):** Direct pairwise head-to-head estimates from clinical trials. Dashes (`—`) indicate unstudied direct comparisons.

```{r table_league, echo=FALSE}
lg_mat <- read.csv("../outputs/tables/league_table_random_common.csv", row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(lg_mat, caption = "Table 2: Complete Dual-Model League Table Matrix")
```

# Methodological Assumption Testing: Inconsistency & Transitivity

## Global Inconsistency Decomposition (Cochran's $Q$)

```{r table_inconsistency, echo=FALSE}
df_inc <- read.csv("../outputs/tables/inconsistency_statistics.csv")
knitr::kable(df_inc, col.names = c("Component", "Q Statistic", "Degrees of Freedom", "p-value", "Assessment"),
             caption = "Table 3: Global Test of Heterogeneity and Inconsistency")
```

*Result:* The between-designs inconsistency test yields $p = 0.8396$, confirming that direct and indirect evidence are coherent across all closed loops of the network.

## Local Inconsistency via Node-Splitting

```{r fig_netsplit, echo=FALSE, out.width="95%"}
knitr::include_graphics("../outputs/figures/04_netsplit_inconsistency.png")
```

Across all evaluated loops, direct and indirect point estimates show overlapping confidence intervals with $p > 0.40$.


# Small-Study Effects & Publication Bias

```{r fig_funnel, echo=FALSE, out.width="90%"}
knitr::include_graphics("../outputs/figures/06_funnel_plot.png")
```

Egger's linear regression test for funnel asymmetry indicates no statistically significant asymmetry ($t = -1.52, p = 0.1374$), confirming symmetric distribution around comparison-specific anchors.

---

# Leave-One-Out (LOO) Influence Cross-Validation

To verify that network estimates are not driven by any single trial, jackknife cross-validation was conducted across all 24 trials.

```{r fig_loo, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%", fig.align='center'}
knitr::include_graphics("../outputs/figures/08_leave_one_out_forest.png")
```

### Empirical Stability Findings
- **Baseline Estimate:** $\text{HR} = 0.687$ ($95\%$ CI: $0.638 - 0.740$).
- **LOO Hazard Ratio Range:** Across all 24 iterations, the estimated HR remained between $0.674$ and $0.707$.
- **Rank 1 Retention:** `Drug C` retained the **#1 hierarchical rank in 100% of iterations (24/24)**.
- **Between-Study Variance:** Heterogeneity remained stable ($\tau^2 \le 0.0002$).

```{r table_loo, echo=FALSE}
if (file.exists("../outputs/tables/leave_one_out_results.csv")) {
  df_loo <- read.csv("../outputs/tables/leave_one_out_results.csv")
  knitr::kable(head(df_loo, 10), caption = "Table 4: Top 10 Influence Iterations from Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation")
}
```

# Component Network Meta-Analysis (CNMA)

Using the additive and interactive component model of Rücker et al. (2020), regimens were deconstructed into constituent components relative to `Component A`:

```{r fig_cnma, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%", fig.align='center'}
knitr::include_graphics("../outputs/figures/09_component_effects.png")
```

### Component Effects & Interaction Testing
- **`Component B` Addition:** $\text{iHR} = 0.711$ ($95\%$ CI: $0.659 - 0.767$, $p < 0.0001$).
- **`Component D` Addition:** $\text{iHR} = 0.845$ ($95\%$ CI: $0.746 - 0.956$, $p = 0.0077$).
- **`Component C` Addition:** $\text{iHR} = 1.056$ ($95\%$ CI: $0.939 - 1.189$, $p = 0.3635$).
- **Interaction Test:** $Q_{\text{diff}} = 15.65$ ($\text{df} = 2$, $p = 0.0004$), indicating significant synergistic interaction beyond linear additivity.

```{r table_cnma, echo=FALSE}
if (file.exists("../outputs/tables/component_nma_effects.csv")) {
  df_cnma <- read.csv("../outputs/tables/component_nma_effects.csv")
  knitr::kable(df_cnma, caption = "Table 5: Incremental Effects of Active Components & Combinations (CNMA)")
}
```

# Bi-dimensional Benefit-Risk Trade-Off Matrix

Survival efficacy is synthesized concurrently with Grade 3–5 severe adverse events across 14,357 patients:

```{r fig_benefit_risk, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%", fig.align='center'}
knitr::include_graphics("../outputs/figures/11_benefit_risk_tradeoff.png")
```

### Quadrant Distribution Summary
1. **Quadrant II (High Efficacy, Low Severe Toxicity):**
   - **`Drug B`:** HR = 0.78 (95% CI: 0.71–0.84), OR = 0.34 (95% CI: 0.28–0.42, $p < 0.0001$).
2. **Quadrant I (High Efficacy, Higher Toxicity):**
   - **`Drug C`:** HR = 0.69 (95% CI: 0.64–0.74), OR = 1.37 (95% CI: 1.16–1.62, $p = 0.0003$).
   - **`Drug D`:** HR = 0.76 (95% CI: 0.69–0.84), OR = 1.01 (95% CI: 0.79–1.28, $p = 0.9636$).
   - **`Drug F`:** HR = 0.72 (95% CI: 0.63–0.83), OR = 1.62 (95% CI: 1.16–2.27, $p = 0.0046$).
3. **Quadrant III (Modest Efficacy, Low Severe Toxicity):**
   - **`Drug E`:** HR = 0.90 (95% CI: 0.82–0.99), OR = 0.29 (95% CI: 0.22–0.38, $p < 0.0001$).
4. **Quadrant IV (Reference Anchor):**
   - **`Drug A`:** Reference backbone ($\text{HR} = 1.00, \text{OR} = 1.00$).

```{r table_benefit_risk, echo=FALSE}
if (file.exists("../outputs/tables/benefit_risk_tradeoff.csv")) {
  df_br <- read.csv("../outputs/tables/benefit_risk_tradeoff.csv")
  knitr::kable(df_br, caption = "Table 7: Bi-dimensional Benefit-Risk Trade-Off Matrix and Net Clinical Benefit")
}
```

# Network Meta-Regression & Transitivity Diagnostics

```{r fig_metareg, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%", fig.align='center'}
knitr::include_graphics("../outputs/figures/12_metaregression_bubble.png")
```

### Moderator Screening Results
- **Publication Year:** $\beta = -0.0037$ (95% CI: -0.0225 to +0.0152, $p = 0.7037$).
- **Trial Sample Size:** $\beta = -0.0454$ (95% CI: -0.1449 to +0.0541, $p = 0.3713$).
- **Geographic Setting:** $\beta = +0.0167$ (95% CI: -0.1322 to +0.1657, $p = 0.8259$).

*Conclusion:* All candidate moderators yielded regression slopes non-significantly different from zero ($p > 0.30$), supporting the transitivity assumption across the network.

```{r table_metareg, echo=FALSE}
if (file.exists("../outputs/tables/metaregression_results.csv")) {
  df_mr <- read.csv("../outputs/tables/metaregression_results.csv")
  knitr::kable(df_mr, caption = "Table 8: Network Meta-Regression Moderator Screening")
}
```

# Subgroup Network Meta-Analysis: Regional Cohorts

Evaluating consistency between Asia-Pacific trials (8 trials, 4,491 patients) and Global trials (16 trials, 11,262 patients):

```{r fig_subgroup, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%", fig.align='center'}
knitr::include_graphics("../outputs/figures/13_subgroup_forest.png")
```

### Between-Subgroups Interaction Testing ($Q_{\text{bws}}$)
- **`Drug C vs Drug A`:** Asia-Pacific $\text{HR} = 0.69$ ($0.59 - 0.82$) vs Global $\text{HR} = 0.68$ ($0.62 - 0.75$) ($Q_{\text{bws}} = 0.0334, df = 1, p = 0.8549$).
- **`Drug F vs Drug A`:** Asia-Pacific $\text{HR} = 0.72$ ($0.59 - 0.87$) vs Global $\text{HR} = 0.75$ ($0.59 - 0.96$) ($Q_{\text{bws}} = 0.0868, df = 1, p = 0.7683$).
- **`Drug E vs Drug A`:** Asia-Pacific $\text{HR} = 0.89$ ($0.80 - 0.99$) vs Global $\text{HR} = 0.98$ ($0.73 - 1.30$) ($Q_{\text{bws}} = 0.3821, df = 1, p = 0.5365$).

*Conclusion:* Between-subgroup testing confirmed regional consistency across all evaluated comparisons ($p > 0.50$).

```{r table_subgroup, echo=FALSE}
if (file.exists("../outputs/tables/subgroup_analysis_results.csv")) {
  df_sg <- read.csv("../outputs/tables/subgroup_analysis_results.csv")
  knitr::kable(df_sg, caption = "Table 9: Subgroup Network Meta-Analysis Contrast Estimates & Between-Subgroups Interaction (Q_bws)")
}
```

# PRISMA-NMA Reporting Compliance Checklist

| Item | PRISMA-NMA Section | Status | Verification in this Monograph |
|:-----|:-------------------|:------:|:--------------------------------|
| **1** | Title | Completed | Explicitly identifies network meta-analysis |
| **2** | Abstract | Completed | Structured executive summary with P-scores and key HRs |

| **15** | Risk of Bias / Diagnostics | Completed | Global $Q_{\text{inc}}$, local node-splitting, Net Heat leverage, LOO |

| **21** | Individual Studies | Completed | Contrast dataset (`data/nsclc_trial_contrasts.csv`) |
| **22** | Sensitivity Analysis | Completed | Leave-One-Out (LOO) cross-validation (Figure 08) |

| **S3** | Benefit-Risk Synthesis | Completed | Dual-outcome efficacy vs severe toxicity decision matrix (Figure 11) |
| **S4** | Transitivity & Meta-Regression | Completed | Network meta-regression across time, sample size, and region (Figure 12) |
| **S5** | Subgroup Synthesis | Completed | Subgroup NMA: Asia-Pacific vs Global trials ($Q_{\text{bws}}$, Figure 13) |
| **S6** | Clinical Significance Framework | Completed | MCID probability engine ($\text{HR} \le 0.80$, Figure 14) |
| **24** | Model Robustness | Completed | Quantitative validation via 24-trial LOO and MCID framework |
